title: How Steve Jobs rebuilt Apple's credibility in a year: the Hierarchy of Skepticism and four great products
summary: At Macworld, interim CEO Jobs borrows Maslow to explain Apple's turnaround as a ladder of skeptic questions: survival, stable business, product strategy, growth. He shows how cutting 15 platforms to four products let Apple put its A team on each, and why brand, design and simplicity drive growth.

principles.text: Cut the lineup to a few great products so your A team can work on every one.
principles.quote: if we only had four, we could put the A team on every single one of them.

principles.text: Fewer products means faster iteration and parallel work on the next generation.
principles.quote: if we only had four, we could turn them all every nine months instead of every eighteen months.

principles.text: Start product strategy from what people actually want, in plain terms, and make it explainable.
principles.quote: So we went back to Business School 101 and said, "What do people want?"

principles.text: If you can't explain your product line to friends, it's too complicated.
principles.quote: How are we going to explain this to others when we don't even know which products to recommend to our friends?

principles.text: Treat each new wave of skepticism as progress: the earlier question has been answered.
principles.quote: it's great, because what it means is we've now convinced them that we've taken care of last month's question—and they're onto the next one.

principles.text: Design and fashion become more important as products go mainstream; design drives demand.
principles.quote: Because of design entering the watch market, today the average American owns seven watches.
